meiofauna.text: Tiny animals that live among the grains of the seafloor.

siphuncle.text: A tube running through the chambers of a cephalopod shell.

bentonite.text: A clay formed from altered volcanic ash.

disaster taxon.text: A species that booms in the wreckage of a mass extinction, spreading widely while competitors are scarce.

plastron.text: The flat bony belly shell of a turtle; the upper shell is the carapace.

tuff.text: Rock made of volcanic ash that has settled and hardened.

konservat-lagerstätte.text: A fossil site of exceptional preservation, where soft tissues and delicate imprints survive.

hyperthermal.text: A rapid, short-lived episode of global warming.

planktic foraminifera.text: Tiny single-celled organisms with shells that drift in the open sea.

polarity reversal.text: A swap of Earth's magnetic north and south poles.

tektite.text: A droplet of natural glass formed from rock melted and thrown out by an impact.

fern spike.text: A sudden burst of fern spores in the fossil record.

diatom.text: A single-celled alga with a glassy shell.

bone conduction.text: Hearing through vibrations carried by the skull bones rather than the eardrum.

maar.text: A crater left by a volcanic explosion, often filled by a lake.

echolocation.text: Sensing the surroundings by sending out sounds and listening for their echoes.

loess.text: Fine, wind-blown silt that piles up in thick blankets.

calcrete.text: A hard, limy crust that forms in soil.

biface.text: A stone tool flaked on both faces, such as a hand axe.

marine isotope stage.text: A numbered warm or cold stage of the ice ages, read from chemical signals in seafloor shells.

thermohaline circulation.text: The deep ocean conveyor driven by differences in heat and salt.

tephra.text: The fragments of rock and ash a volcano hurls into the air.

hafting.text: Fixing a stone point or blade to a handle or shaft.

fire-stick farming.text: The deliberate burning of forest and grassland to shape the landscape.

refugium.text: A sheltered area where species survive a harsh period such as a glacial maximum.

phreatomagmatic eruption.text: An eruption driven by steam where magma meets water.

polar seesaw.text: A pattern in which one hemisphere warms while the other cools.

surface mass balance.text: The yearly gain of snow on an ice sheet minus what it loses to melting.

perihelion.text: The point in Earth's orbit where it passes closest to the Sun.

sapropel.text: A dark, organic-rich mud laid down on the sea floor when bottom waters lose oxygen.

post-glacial rebound.text: The slow rise of the Earth's crust after the weight of an ice sheet is removed.

coral bleaching.text: The whitening of heat-stressed corals that expel the algae living in them.
